system_overview: This specification models the Tower of Hanoi puzzle using a bitwise representation of disk positions. The Tower of Hanoi is a mathematical puzzle consisting of a configurable number of disks of distinct sizes and a configurable number of towers (pegs). All disks start stacked on the first tower in order of size (largest at the bottom). The objective is to move all disks to the last tower, subject to the constraint that only one disk may be moved at a time and no disk may be placed on top of a smaller disk. The minimum number of moves to solve an n-disk puzzle is 2^n - 1.
actors_and_components: There are no concurrent actors. The system is a single-player puzzle. The components are D disks of sizes that are powers of two (1, 2, 4, ..., 2^(D-1)) and N towers.
state_variables: The system maintains an array of N tower values, one per tower. Each tower's value is a natural number whose binary representation encodes which disks are on that tower: bit position k is set if the disk of size 2^k is present on that tower. A tower value of zero means the tower is empty. The sum of all tower values always equals 2^D - 1 (all disks are accounted for).
initial_state: All disks are on the first tower (its value is 2^D - 1, meaning all bits are set). All other towers are empty (value zero).
actions: A single move action selects a disk (which must be a power of two), a source tower, and a destination tower. The move is valid if: (1) the disk is on the source tower (the corresponding bit is set), (2) the disk is the smallest disk on the source tower (all lower-order bits are zero), and (3) the destination tower has no disk smaller than the one being moved (all lower-order bits are zero) or is empty. When a move occurs, the disk's value is subtracted from the source tower and added to the destination tower.
safety_properties: Conservation: the sum of all tower values equals 2^D - 1 at all times (no disks are created or destroyed). Type correctness: all tower values are natural numbers less than 2^D.
liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED. The specification does not assert liveness. Instead, the puzzle is solved by checking whether the negation of the goal state (all disks on the last tower) is an invariant; a counterexample trace produced by the model checker demonstrates the solution.
model_bounds: D (number of disks) and N (number of towers) are declared as constants. For model checking, typical values are D=3 and N=3, which requires 7 moves to solve.
additional_assumptions: Disks are represented as powers of two, and tower state is encoded as the sum of present disk values. Bitwise AND is used to test disk presence and ordering constraints; this requires a custom operator module that implements bitwise AND either in pure arithmetic or via a Java override class. The specification does not enforce a strategy; all legal moves are explored nondeterministically.
